history.heading: Mossi kingdoms
paragraphs: The region of present-day Burkina Faso was home to farming peoples for thousands of years. From the 11th to 15th centuries, the Mossi founded several powerful kingdoms, the most important being Ouagadougou, ruled by the Mogho Naba. The Mossi resisted the expanding empires of Mali and Songhai.
The Ruins of Loropéni in the southwest, a stone-walled settlement linked to the gold trade, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

history.heading: Colony of Upper Volta
paragraphs: France conquered the region in the 1890s. The colony of Upper Volta was created in 1919, dissolved in 1932 and divided among neighbouring colonies, then re-established in 1947. It served largely as a source of labour for plantations in Ivory Coast.

history.heading: Independence and Thomas Sankara
paragraphs: Upper Volta became independent on 5 August 1960 and experienced several coups. In 1983 Captain Thomas Sankara took power and launched a revolutionary programme promoting self-reliance, women's rights, vaccination and anti-corruption. In 1984 he renamed the country Burkina Faso, meaning "land of upright people".

Sankara was killed in a 1987 coup led by Blaise Compaoré, who ruled for 27 years until a popular uprising forced him out in 2014. Since 2015, jihadist insurgency has spread across the country, killing thousands and displacing over two million people. Two military coups in 2022 brought Captain Ibrahim Traoré to power.

culture.heading: Peoples and arts
paragraphs: Burkina Faso has more than 60 ethnic groups; the Mossi are the largest. French is official, and Mooré, Dioula and Fulfulde are widely spoken. Islam is the largest religion, followed by Christianity and traditional beliefs, with a long tradition of religious tolerance.

Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival, held every two years, and SIAO, a major international crafts fair. Masks, bronze casting and music are important traditions. The staple food is tô, a thick millet or maize porridge served with sauces.

politics.heading: Military rule
paragraphs: Burkina Faso is governed by a military junta that took power in 2022. The transition period was extended to 2029, political parties were dissolved in 2025, and critics of the government have faced conscription or arrest.
The junta expelled French troops and turned toward Russia for security cooperation. With Mali and Niger, it formed the Alliance of Sahel States and left the regional bloc ECOWAS in January 2025.

economy.heading: Gold and cotton
paragraphs: Most people work in subsistence agriculture and livestock raising. Gold has become the main export, from industrial mines and artisanal mining, followed by cotton. The government has moved to increase state control of gold mines.
Burkina Faso uses the West African CFA franc. It is among the world's poorest countries, and the insurgency has disrupted farming, closed schools and health centres and displaced many people.
